generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a thick, fibrous trunk of matted roots growing a few centimetres a year to 4 to 5 m, under a spreading crown of twice-divided fronds 2 to 3 m long that unroll from hairy croziers in spring; dead fronds hang in a skirt. Native to south-eastern Australia and Tasmania. Not fitted to measurements. Refitted from Hoshizaki and Moran (2001, p. 16, 109, 111, 281-283) and the research note's web sources: the trunk is about 25 to 30 cm across below the crown, its mantle of matted roots and old stipe bases widening it toward the foot (to 1 m or more in old plants), so a radius of 0.13 m thickening by 1.2 of itself over about fifty years; fronds live about two years; a crozier coils one and a half to three turns (Kaplan 2022, p. 346), so each coiled piece turns 100 degrees. Hoshizaki and Moran (2001, pp. 281, 283): the blade is narrowed at the base, widest above the middle (oblanceolate), so pinnae longest at 0.6 of the rachis (leaflet_peak) and the lowest a fifth of the longest (leaflet_base). Growing fronds lean 25 degrees from the vertical as they open into the spreading crown (young_angle, by eye).

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 2.5 m at 30 years and 4 m at 60. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Hoshizaki and Moran (2001, p. 282): D. antarctica's stipes lose their hairs early, with tan or green rachises (leaf_axis a tan green). Colours otherwise chosen by eye from photographs: mid-green fronds, a dark brown fibrous trunk.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.
